payload: Seven everyday things you can do easily if you probably do NOT have AuDHD (combined autism + ADHD), framed as a Jeff-Foxworthy-style 'you might not be' quiz built on the idea of two opposing brain operating systems -- ADHD craving novelty/chaos and autism craving structure/routine -- constantly at war. If each of these is a struggle rather than easy, that internal war is the tell.

points.label: You actually use the planner you bought
points.detail: You buy a planner, fill it out, and keep using it; for AuDHD the autistic side plans it while the ADHD side rebels and sabotages it by Wednesday.

points.label: Your brain has an off switch at night
points.detail: Bedtime is a calm 10-minute transition; for AuDHD both sides gang up -- sensory hyper-awareness plus a 1am hyperfixation (e.g. competitive cheese rolling) leaving you wired.

points.label: You're fine winging it
points.detail: You can enter a meeting without full info and think 'we'll figure it out'; for AuDHD the lack of a script triggers panic/a black-hole dread.

points.label: You're carefree and adventurous
points.detail: You can pack a bag for a spontaneous trip without spiraling; the AuDHD autistic side mentally unpacks it and demands routine and pre-approved plans.

points.label: Socializing energizes you
points.detail: Party-hopping and crowds leave you energized for the week; for AuDHD small talk and noise cause a meltdown, draining you for days.

points.label: Buying a simple item takes five minutes
points.detail: You just buy what you need instead of a multi-day research project with three-star-review reading and comparison spreadsheets (the creator took 14 months to buy a car).

points.label: Friendships are easy to start and keep
points.detail: For AuDHD, ADHD 'out of sight, out of mind' plus time blindness plus autistic guilt over friendship rules erodes contact for months or years.

notes: Promises seven and delivers all seven, in order.
Framing conflates ADHD and AuDHD: items 1-3 say 'you might not be ADHD' but the payoff/thesis is AuDHD (autism + ADHD together, 'two opposing operating systems').
Verdict line: if your brain constantly wages war between wanting total structure and total chaos, you're probably AuDHD; ends with a CTA to comment your result and watch another video.
gaps: A self-diagnostic entertainment quiz with no clinical criteria or professional-evaluation disclaimer; relatable traits are presented as diagnostic signals.
